selection.name: example PV installation
selection.description: the default installation of the page: 10 kWp east-west on a flat roof in the Swiss plateau, a 10 kWh battery and a household that uses 4500 kWh a year; every input can be changed, the numbers of this phrase are the worked example

description: Use case: the main results of a rooftop photovoltaic installation in Switzerland over its lifetime, the electricity produced and the CO2-eq saved against the Swiss consumption mix and against a replacement mix, as shown by the system view 'Calculator' for the phrase 'example PV installation'; the inputs, the assumptions, the result rows, the detail table, the labels and the hints of the page are the calculator triples of 'PV installation' and the general calculator triples of the listed phrases. The inputs are the system size in kWp, the orientation as a yield factor, the usable battery capacity and the annual household consumption; the worked example is 10 kWp east-west, 10 kWh battery, 4500 kWh. Every delivered kWh, used at home or exported, is assumed to displace one kWh of the reference mix; the embodied emission of the PV system (IEA PVPS 2023 reference, converted to a fixed amount per kWp) and of the batteries bought over the lifetime is subtracted. The CO2-eq saving is stated three times: with the annual Swiss consumption mix of 2018 (KBOB), with the monthly Swiss consumption mix 2018 to 2022 (treeze) weighted by the PV electricity delivered in each month, which is lower because PV produces in summer when the Swiss mix is cleanest, and with the European residual mix (Swissolar) as the replacement mix. The monthly dispatch of the page (direct use capped by the day share of the consumption, battery charge capped by one cycle a day and the night consumption) needs a minimum function, so its two annual sums and the PV-weighted mix are stored as modelled values; all other results are formulas of the file and reproduced by the calc-validation. The inputs that are not measured carry the word assumed and a confidence.

formulas.name: PV production by orientation
formulas.description: the annual PV production: the rated power times the specific yield of the best orientation times the yield factor of the real orientation

formulas.name: battery discharge formula
formulas.description: what the battery gives back: the charge times the round-trip efficiency

formulas.name: export formula
formulas.description: the PV production that is neither used directly nor stored goes to the grid

formulas.name: grid import formula
formulas.description: the consumption not covered by direct use and battery discharge is bought from the grid

formulas.name: delivered electricity formula
formulas.description: the PV electricity that reaches a consumer, so the production minus the battery losses

formulas.name: self-consumption share by dispatch
formulas.description: the share of the production used on site; the battery charge counts in full, because the losses happen on site too. The self-consumption model has a monthly resolution: the direct use is capped at the load during the PV hours, the battery does at most one full cycle per day and only covers the evening and night load. Real day-to-day weather swings lower the battery share somewhat. The monthly PV and load profiles are assumed typical values for the Zurich region (confidence 0.6)

formulas.name: autarky formula
formulas.description: the share of the household consumption covered by the own PV electricity

formulas.name: PV embodied intensity formula
formulas.description: turns the life cycle emission per kWh of the reference system into a fixed amount per kWp: the emission per kWh is spread over the reference yield and lifetime, so a site with a lower yield has the same embodied emission and a higher emission per kWh; the division by 1000 converts gram to kg

formulas.name: battery embodied emission formula
formulas.description: the production emission of all batteries bought over the lifetime
formulas.expression: "battery embodied emission" = "battery capacity" * "battery production emission" * "battery count"

formulas.name: gross avoided emission by consumption mix
formulas.description: the emission of the Swiss consumption mix that the delivered PV electricity displaces over the lifetime; one formula per reference mix, because the mix is the operand; the division by 1000 converts gram to kg

formulas.name: gross avoided emission by PV-weighted consumption mix
formulas.description: the same with the Swiss consumption mix weighted by the monthly PV delivery: PV produces mostly in summer, when the Swiss consumption mix is cleanest (about 70 to 90 g/kWh in May to August, 140 to 165 g/kWh in winter), so weighting the PV output of each month by the mix of that month gives a lower saving than the annual average

formulas.name: gross avoided emission by residual mix
formulas.description: the same with the European residual mix as the replacement mix

formulas.name: net avoided emission formula
formulas.description: the gross avoided emission minus the embodied emission of the PV system and the battery; the reference mix is selected by the context. Every PV kilowatt-hour that reaches a consumer, used at home or exported, is assumed to displace one kilowatt-hour of grid electricity, the production emissions of the modules and the battery are subtracted, and the battery losses reduce the delivered energy
formulas.expression: "net avoided emission" = "gross avoided emission" - "PV embodied emission" - "battery embodied emission"

formulas.name: emission payback formula
formulas.description: the operating years until the gross avoided emission equals the embodied emission, assuming an even avoided emission per year
formulas.expression: "emission payback" = ( "PV embodied emission" + "battery embodied emission" ) / "gross avoided emission" * "lifetime"

formulas.name: lifetime total formula
formulas.description: the total of an annual number over the lifetime of the installation, e.g. the PV production or the export; the result carries the lifetime word in place of the annual word of the input, and the years are the lifetime of the PV installation

formulas.name: annual share formula
formulas.description: the share of one year of a CO2-eq total over the lifetime, e.g. the embodied emission of the PV system or the net avoided emission; the result carries the annual word, and the years are the lifetime of the PV installation

formulas.name: battery losses formula
formulas.description: the battery losses: the charge minus what the battery gives back

formulas.name: battery effect formula
formulas.description: the effect of the battery on the net avoided emission against the same PV installation without battery, which delivers all its production: the lifetime battery losses do not displace the reference mix and the battery production adds its embodied emission; the division by 1000 converts gram to kg

formulas.name: PV site intensity formula
formulas.description: the embodied emission of the PV system divided by the lifetime production at this site; the multiplication by 1000 converts kg to gram

formulas.name: gross avoided emission by production mix
formulas.description: the same with the European production mix as the replacement mix

formulas.name: annual consumption mix by PV weighting
formulas.description: the consumption mix of a year as the PV installation uses it: the PV-weighted consumption mix, so that the year row of the monthly table shows the mix that the twelve monthly mixes give with the PV delivery as the weight
